symptoms: Even green colour with no spots, patches, curling or mould on the leaf.
prevention: Water at the base of plants rather than over the leaves.
Rotate crops and remove old plant debris after harvest.
management_guidance: Continue regular field scouting; healthy-looking leaves can still hide early infection.
next_steps: Keep checking plants weekly, including the undersides of leaves.
If symptoms appear later, take a new clear photo and scan again.

symptoms: Dark brown spots, often with concentric rings like a target.
Older, lower leaves are usually affected first.
Yellowing around spots; leaves may drop.
prevention: Remove and destroy infected plant debris.
Avoid overhead irrigation and avoid wetting leaves late in the day.
Stake or mulch plants to reduce soil splash.
management_guidance: Remove badly affected lower leaves where practical.
Ask your agricultural officer which locally approved product and schedule is appropriate for your field.
next_steps: Compare the leaf with the symptoms listed here and check several plants, not just one.
Show the plant or a clear photo to your local agricultural officer or Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) before choosing any treatment.
Do not spray any chemical based only on this app's result.

symptoms: Large, irregular, water-soaked or greasy-looking patches that turn brown/black.
White fuzzy growth may appear on leaf undersides in humid weather.
Can spread very quickly in cool, wet conditions and also affects stems and fruit.
prevention: Avoid dense planting and long leaf-wetness periods.
Remove volunteer tomato and potato plants nearby.
management_guidance: Late blight can spread fast: seek expert advice promptly instead of waiting.
Remove and safely dispose of severely infected plants as advised locally.
next_steps: Treat this as potentially serious and contact your agricultural officer or KVK soon.
Avoid moving between infected and healthy plants without cleaning tools and hands.

symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots that may become slightly raised or scabby.
Spots can have a yellow halo; severe cases cause leaf drop.
Fruit may show rough, raised spots.
prevention: Use clean seed and healthy seedlings.
Avoid working in the field when plants are wet.
management_guidance: Remove and dispose of infected plant material carefully.
Ask your agricultural officer about locally approved options; bacterial diseases are often hard to control once established.

symptoms: Pale green or yellow patches on the upper leaf surface.
Olive-green to grey-brown mould on the underside of the matching patches.
Common in warm, humid, poorly ventilated conditions.
prevention: Improve ventilation and spacing, including in greenhouses or tunnels.
Avoid wetting leaves and keep humidity down.
Remove old infected leaves and debris.
management_guidance: Reduce humidity and leaf wetness first.
Ask your agricultural officer which locally approved product, if any, is suitable.
